<reason>Both sides built coherent cases and executed the pressure-question mechanic properly (clear A1:/A2: labeling on both sides), but B ultimately controlled the decisive exchange. A's sharpest move was catching that B's own stigma-fix (building-level community eligibility) is itself targeting, forcing B to defend granularity rather than pure universalism — a genuinely clever catch. But B answered it with the basement-apartment/mixed-district example, and A's counter (individual-level data-matching everywhere) drew a real concession in Rebuttal 2 ("the remaining sliver... is a real design problem"). B's closing weaponized that concession relentlessly and effectively ("she goes hungry all year while the model performs beautifully on average"), and A never fully recovered from it, instead re-asserting that the sliver is narrow without giving a compelling reason a targeted "fix later" beats "feed her now." On the money/political-economy sub-debate, A's statutory-line-item citation was a fair answer to B's bus/library analogy, but B's rebuttal — that verification apparatuses function as a hidden dial legislators use to shrink programs without repealing them — was a more concrete mechanism, and A's Rebuttal 2 never directly answered B's pressure question about what rule guarantees crowd-out savings actually reach backpack/breakfast programs; B correctly called this unanswered and A's closing didn't repair it. That live, unrebutted hole, combined with B's stronger, more memorable closing framing of the asymmetric error costs, gives B the clearer path to victory, though the debate stayed competitive throughout with each side landing real hits.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The decisive exchange was A's Rebuttal 2 concession that "the remaining sliver... is a real design problem" (A4.2), which B's closing seized on to argue that targeting inherently fails identifiable, individual children while promising future fixes — a framing A's closing never fully neutralized, especially since A also left B's crowd-out "what rule guarantees redirection" pressure question effectively unanswered.</best_rebuttal>
